text:
paul: PSA from baggage claim chaos  my fragile souvenir mug did not survive the flight. Rest in pieces. 62d Anyone have quick tips to protect fragile gifts for future offsites?
yvonne: Oh no! So sad. For fragile ceramics, I wrap in clean socks (saves space) then bubble wrap, then layer between clothes in the center of the bag.
marco: If it's fragile, carry it on. Worst-case: box it in a gift bag and gate-check if its huge. Also use "Fragile" stickers on the outside. Not foolproof but helps.
lina: Photo everything for claims. Take close-ups of the broken item, inside/outside of the suitcase, and the baggage tag. Email to the airline ASAP.
claims-bot: Airline claim tip: file within 24h for domestic flights, 7 days for damage on many carriers. Keep receipts if you want reimbursement. Link: https://airline.example/claims
yvonne: Also put a soft layer like a beach towel around fragile things, then place them between shoes or socks so they don't shift. Use compression cubes as stabilizers.
marco: Pro packing hack: put fragile in the middle, surround with rolled clothes, then wear the bulkiest coat to the airport and stuff heavier shoes on the outside of the bag.
nina: (jk not nina, lin a) If an item breaks, sometimes the airport lost-and-found keeps smaller parts. Worth asking.
paul: Filed a claim. Hoping for a partial refund but mostly sad about the novelty mug. Also guilty about cheap packing on my end.
yvonne: For future offsites, can we do a "souvenir registry" in the travel thread? If people want fragile local items, we can share shipping addresses before traveling, or the team can assign someone to hand-carry.
marco: Love this idea. Or an offsite "swap table" where people can bring small items and put them in protective sleeves. No broken treasures allowed. :no_good:
travel-desk-bot: Note added to travel checklist: "fragile items guidance + optional 'carry-on courier' sign-up". Link: https://drive.example/travel-guides
paul: Also, small tip for claims: include a photo of the item's original packaging/receipt if you have it. Airlines are weird about proof of value.
lina: If you're buying mugs/small glass in souvenir shops, ask for extra bubble wrap or the shop's cardboard box. Many shops will box it up for free.
marco: And if anyones bringing local alcohol bottles, remember EU/UK rules for liquids and check customs limits if crossing borders. Also pad them heavily.
yvonne: Group consensus: fragile = carry-on when possible; if checked, double-wrap + inner padding + photo proof + label as fragile. Also, bring a tiny glue kit for emergency bonding.
paul: Thanks all. Appreciate the empathy and pro tips. Will volunteer as the official team mug courier next time 604
claims-bot: Claim submitted: case #CL-2026-889. Please keep receipts and follow up via the airline portal.
marco: Also, for levity: proposing a team tradition  bring one non-breakable local trinket for the shared office "world shelf" so we avoid flying ceramics. Vote with :thumbsup: if youre in.
yvonne: :thumbsup: from me. Cheaper and sturdier souvenirs FTW.
paul: :thumbsup: I'll bring a wooden magnet next time.
